newsitem.title: USA: Solv-Ex to apply for 100,000 bpd permit.
newsitem.headline: Solv-Ex to apply for 100,000 bpd permit.

text.p: Solv-Ex Corp said it will apply mid-year for a permit to produce 100,000 barrels per day of oil, the company's chairman and chief executive officer, John Rendall told a teleconference Monday.
Rendall said Solv-Ex Corp's oil production cost will be third of the current market price of about $20 per barrel.

Solv-Ex will begin production of bitumen from Athabasca oil sands in Canada mid-March at the rate of 3,500 barrels per day or 25 percent of capacity, building up to 14,000 barrels per day within six months, Rendall said.

The bitumen will be blended with condensate initially. Equipment will then be installed so that by the end of the year, the product will be of 22 degrees gravity and pipelineable, a Solv-Ex official explained later.
A sulphuric acid plant will also be built during the second and third quarters to leach alumina and a titanium dioxide subsitute from the Athabasca clays from the fourth quarter, Rendall added.
Rendall said the original plan had been to start up part of the oil production plant in February, but following advice, it was decided to start the whole plant slightly later.
"By the middle of the year we will be applying for a permit for 100,000 barrels per day of production," Rendall added.
"We believe the permit hearings will not be as lengthy as otherwise because of our environmental advantages."
There will be a "pipeline available by the end of next year for the oil to flow out from out site", Rendall added.
